name: Live Integration Radar
summary: Can unfinished agent work reveal a composition problem before the tasks are complete?
problem: Parallel changes can pass their own tests and still fail when combined. Operators spend time making those changes fit together.
idea: Test exact combinations of work-in-progress heads and deliver evidence-bound warnings to the agents while they can still change course.
evidence: The equal-policy live pair produced compatible first source commits, no notices, and zero subsequent source repairs in both arms. Both principals withdrew the primary recommendation. This result does not establish warning uptake or prove that interference never occurs.
test: A useful neutral task family where a real agent discovers and consumes a warning. Preserve immutable candidate heads and compare against completion-time checks with equal task policy.
falsifier: If agents do not change useful outcomes or measured repair effort compared with ordinary worktrees and final integration tests, this should remain a capability rather than the primary product.

name: Storage-aware workspaces
summary: Keep writable tasks isolated without multiplying dependencies and build footprints.
problem: Alexey’s linked worktrees grew quickly on disk. A scan of one host found 111.7 GiB across 472 worktrees, with dependencies and builds accounting for 62.1% of the physical union.
idea: Account for source, immutable dependencies, mutable outputs, caches, and logs separately. Compare ordinary package sharing, sparse or copy-on-write worktrees, and remote execution without hiding allocation costs.
evidence: The corrected tiny-task N2 experiment measured normalized whole-footprint savings of 48.17%, below the registered greater-than-50% gate. Sharing mechanisms and isolation limits are still being tested. No existing worktrees were authorized for deletion.
test: Equivalent real coding tasks and accepted build/test outcomes, with unique allocated bytes including stores and caches. Test mutations, independent source edits, recovery, and actual guard behavior.
falsifier: If ordinary package and workspace lifecycle tools solve the pain with less complexity, an Artifacts-specific local product may not be needed. A useful workspace diagnostic could still survive.

name: Behavior-based fork tournament
summary: Choose between parallel attempts by what they do, with a bounded and independent review.
problem: People already using best-of-N agents must compare attempts, identify behavior that is wrong, and safely land the useful result.
idea: Run the same versioned task in a few forks, compare accepted behavior and independent checks, allow ties or neither, and preserve the losing attempts with their evidence.
evidence: This remains a hypothesis supported by reports from existing best-of-N users. A comparative live trial and advantage over current vendor selection workflows have not been demonstrated.
test: Compare a single attempt and existing vendor-style selection on a declared small task set. Give reviewers equal test evidence and measure accepted outcomes, review effort, and usage.
falsifier: Equal outcomes with higher model usage, review burden, or operational complexity are grounds to park it.

name: Change-story review
summary: A short account of behavioral changes, tied to the evidence a reviewer actually needs.
problem: Reviewers remain responsible for quality as coding agents create more changes. A longer generated summary can increase work or anchor a reviewer on an inaccurate story.
idea: Connect a task contract, exact diff, tested behavior, impacted consumers, and evidence links in a concise review artifact. Keep transcripts optional.
evidence: Review pain is supported by the research. Generic navigation and snapshots overlap incumbent capabilities. An internal decision card has been used, but that is not a blind timing comparison, improved defect catch, or external demand.
test: A prospective unfamiliar review decision with equal evidence and an ordinary PR-list control. Measure review effort and defect catch without manufacturing a helpful bug.
falsifier: If a story hides a defect, biases the reviewer, or fails to reduce effort with equal quality, a generated summary is not an improvement.

name: Durable task handoff
summary: Resume the right task on the right code state without reconstructing an entire conversation.
problem: An agent restart or replacement can lose intent, unfinished work, acceptance criteria, or awareness that the canonical branch has advanced.
idea: Keep a versioned task manifest with exact base and current SHAs, unresolved decisions, actual checks, and a receiver acknowledgement. Exclude private traces and credentials.
evidence: Structured handoffs and ordinary Git recovery offer plausible mechanisms. Existing checkpoint and session-resume products are strong controls; metadata storage alone is not novel. Comparative recovery and live gates remain open.
test: Restart and drift tasks compared with native session resume, checkpoints, and git log plus a structured plan. Include permitted dirty or untracked work and stale-owner cases.
falsifier: If correct-base recovery, preserved acceptance, time, and review effort do not improve over ordinary tools, avoid adding another coordination layer.
